bcwsft

An R port of the BC Wildfire Service fuel-typing algorithm: the expert decision tree of Perrakis, Eade & Hicks (2018) that assigns Canadian FBP System fuel types to VRI polygons from forest-inventory attributes.

This is a faithful translation of Gregory A. Greene’s Python implementation bcwft2018, with no ArcGIS / arcpy dependency (the Python core is pure pandas/numpy; only the optional I/O wrappers used arcpy, and those are not ported). It is intended as an independent, scriptable cross-check on map-derived fuel-type products such as the BC Wildfire “Fire Fuel Types - Public” layer.

License

GPL-3. This package is a derivative work of GPL-3 code (bcwft2018.py) and so must remain GPL-3. Apache-2.0 / MIT projects may depend on and call this package (e.g. via bcwsft::bcwsft_fuel_type()) without changing their own license, provided they do not copy this package’s source into their tree. See LICENSE.md.

Status

Component State
Input validation, constants (species/BEC lists) ported (hand)
Predicates (is_vegetated, is_logged, harv_lag, pct_conifer, …) ported (hand)
Decision tree: non-vegetated branch (bcwft2018.py ~L402-487) ported
Decision tree: vegetated branch (~L488-1859) ported (transpiled)

The decision tree (R/decision-tree.R) is generated from the reference Python by data-raw/transpile.py and validated against the reference output across thousands of random VRI rows (0 mismatches; see data-raw/). Rows whose required inventory attributes are missing error out, matching the reference; use on_error = "na" to get NA for such rows instead.

Usage 

library(bcwsft)

vri <- data.frame(
  BCLCS_LEVEL_1 = "N", COAST_INTERIOR_CD = "I", BEC_ZONE_CODE = "ICH",
  BEC_SUBZONE = "mc", HARVEST_DATE = "2018-06-01", SPECIES_CD_1 = "PL",
  SPECIES_PCT_1 = 80 # ... plus the remaining bcwsft_input_columns
)
bcwsft_fuel_type(vri, season = "growing", current_year = 2024)
#>   branch                              fuel_type ft_modifier
#> 1 NV/logged/harv<=24/other/growing    O-1b      NA

bcwsft_input_columns lists every VRI attribute the algorithm consumes.

Validating against the reference implementation

The golden-output test compares this port to Greene’s Python tool row-for-row. To generate the reference output (requires Python + pandas/numpy and a clone of the original repo; no ArcGIS licence needed):

python data-raw/generate_golden.py /path/to/BC_CFFBPS_FuelTyping_Tool
# writes tests/testthat/fixtures/golden_output.csv
R -e 'testthat::test_local()'

If golden_output.csv is absent the golden test skips; the unit tests for the ported branches (with a pinned current_year) always run.
